messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — DNS resolution skew detected between Route53 and Cloudflare. Significant 5xx spike observed in eu-1 and apac-1 regions. Paging on-call SRE.

pagerduty: Alert routed to leo (oncall-sre). Escalation policy: network -> eng-platform if not ack within 2m.

leo: acked. oncall here — looking. anyone know if we rolled a DNS change recently?

jen: I pushed a DNS change earlier to remove the CNAME for api.redwood.ai and replace with an ALIAS to wrangler-managed proxy. Change went to Route53 at 10:02 UTC, supposed to be synced to Cloudflare via external sync job.

priya: API: netops — we saw the sync job report success, but probes show different answers from public resolvers. grabbing dig results now.

priya: dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short -> 10.2.3.4

priya: dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +short -> 52.45.11.10

matt: that's the problem — Route53 is returning 10.2.3.4 (new) and Cloudflare still answering 52.45.11.10 (old). Some resolvers are wired to CF, some to R53, causing client requests to hit different backends.

sam: customer-impact: support dashboard shows elevated 502/504 from customers routed through eu and apac edge. Tentative impact: ~3.1% of requests in last 10m, concentrated for customers on eu-1 and apac-1. CS already getting tickets.

jen: can we quickly measure where the mismatches are? running aws route53 list-resource-record-sets and cf api dump.

jen: route53 record (current):
```
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 10.2.3.4
```

jen: cloudflare edge config (current):
```
api.redwood.ai -> 52.45.11.10 (proxy)
```

leo: looks like the sync job partially applied. maybe a race: TTL lowered after update and some resolvers cached the old IP. Any chance the ALIAS isn't compatible with CF proxy?

priya: checking sync logs — sync completed, but our CF worker returned 200 while doing on-the-fly transform and ignored the ALIAS -> left the old A record. filing a ticket with the sync maintainer.

matt: mitigation plan: short-term: 1) roll back Route53 to the old A record (52.45.11.10) so answers converge, 2) invalidate Cloudflare edge caches / purge DNS if possible, 3) keep TTL low while we fix sync job and re-deploy change. Thoughts?

leo: +1 rollback now. if we unify to the old IP, customer requests will stabilize while we coordinate a safe migration.

jen: rolling back Route53 now.

jen: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://rollback.json

jen: change submitted. Change ID xyz123. Expected propagation ~60s-5m.

priya: contacting Cloudflare support to confirm their DNS entries and request any immediate flushes. pinging Cloudflare-Support channel.

cloudflare-support: Hi team — we saw your ticket. Cloudflare authoritative records show old A record; no purge required on our side. We can force re-propagation on our edge but that usually isn't necessary — the inconsistency is due to mixed resolvers returning data from different upstreams.

sam: monitoring: beginning to see 5xx counts drop in eu-1 after Route53 rollback submission. current impact down from 3.1% to 0.9% in last 5m.

leo: good. continuing monitoring. assign netops to own follow-up to debug the sync job. handing off incident to priya for mitigation and postmortem.

leo: handoff note: oncall-sre -> priya (netops). Incident state: mitigated but not resolved. Need root cause (sync race), verify no other records affected, and implement guardrails.

priya: acked and taking over. immediate actions: 1) validate sync job codepath that handles ALIAS/CNAME/A records, 2) add end-to-end preflight check before applying changes (compare CF vs R53 answers), 3) add canary window for DNS changes, 4) reduce TTLs on critical records during migration windows.

matt: also add alerting on divergence: if authoritative answers between providers differ for a record, fire a warning. We missed that earlier.

sam: customer comms: drafting status update for affected customers — saying we observed DNS inconsistency affecting EU/APAC with transient 5xxs and that we rolled back to stabilize. ETA for follow-up: 2–4 hours for full remediation plan.

jen: note: rollback change completed at change status INSYNC (Route53). Confirmed via dig from multiple doh endpoints now all returning 52.45.11.10.

priya: we reproduced a failure mode locally: when sync job runs concurrently with a manual rollover it can create a temporary state where CF retains old record while R53 flips. Sync job assumed idempotent but a transformation step returned stale payload. Patch incoming.

priya: created PR that adds a compare-and-swap step and an end-to-end verification before marking sync success. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/dns-sync/pull/412

leo: good. let's schedule a controlled re-apply after PR and deploy, with oncall monitoring and a strict rollback plan.

matt: action items captured:
- priya: own sync PR + deploy + add preflight checks (P0)
- eng-platform (matt/jen): add divergence alerting and a canary workflow for DNS changes (P1)
- support (sam): finalize customer comms and update support tickets (P2)
- oncall-sre (leo): write runbook for DNS-change rollback and verification (P2)

sam: preliminary impact estimate for postmortem: ~45m of elevated errors for a subset of customers; peak affected requests ~3.1%; ~12 support tickets opened in window. I'll collate logs for the notes.

cloudflare-support: we can assist with TTL and any manual edge clears if needed during the controlled reapply. ping us before you re-run the migration.

leo: closing handoff. status: mitigated -> monitored. priya owns next steps. I'll remain available during the reapply window.

priya: thanks. will schedule reapply tomorrow 03:00 UTC in a canary fashion. Will post an update here once PR deployed and first canary completed.

matt: agree. postmortem owners: priya + matt. timeline and follow-up due in 72h.

jen: thanks all — glad we stabilized.

sam: support status: customer-facing note queued.

leo: incident thread closed for active paging. Reopen if divergence reappears.

[automated-note] incident-bot: incident marked 'mitigated' at 1749877840. Postmortem scheduled.
